transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. Um... I guess I came in because... well, I know this sounds a bit hard to explain, and I really hope I don't sound completely unreasonable. I'm sure it's mostly just me overthinking things, but... I've been completely convinced lately that one of my MBA classmates and a startup advisor are sort of quietly coordinating opportunities for me. 

Like... it feels like certain comments they make in class, or even just regular Slack messages, are actually these coded signals about where my career is supposed to go. I know that probably sounds a little silly to bring up, right? I just wanted to check in and make sure I'm processing everything appropriately, if that makes sense?
How long have you been feeling like your classmate and the startup advisor are sending you coded signals?

Um... I'd say it's been going on for about two months? It started right around the time I began the part-time MBA prerequisite program. I've been keeping my regular operations job while doing the classes, so... I guess I've been a little stretched thin lately. 

I really think it's probably just the stress of juggling both things that's making me read way too much into their comments, you know? Does that sound like a normal reaction to you? I really hope I'm not wasting your time with something that's just... regular work stress.
Have you been having any other thoughts that feel like people are sending you hidden messages or that something unusual is going on that others might not be aware of?

Oh, um... no, definitely not. It's really just... just that one specific situation with my classmate and the advisor. I haven't felt like anyone else is doing anything like that—not at my regular job, or, you know, with my friends or family or anything. 

I think if it was happening everywhere, I'd be a lot more worried, right? But since it's just tied to the MBA classes... I'm hoping it really is just me overanalyzing a new, competitive environment. That's a good sign, isn't it? That it's just isolated to that one specific thing? I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture and not making it sound worse than it actually is.
How certain are you that your classmate and the startup advisor are actually sending you coded signals?

Um... well... I guess if I'm being completely honest, part of me is really, truly convinced that it's actually happening. Like, in the moment, when I see a message or hear a comment, it feels so real and deliberate, you know? 

But then... well, then I step back and think about how it sounds out loud, and I realize it might seem a bit much. I mean, I don't want to seem like I'm totally out of touch with reality or anything. I know it's probably just my mind playing tricks on me because I'm so eager to do well in the program. 

So, I guess I'm... I'm pretty convinced when it happens, but I'm also trying really hard to be logical about it. Does that make sense? I really hope I'm explaining this in a way that shows I'm still trying to stay grounded. Is it okay that I feel both ways about it?
How much distress or anxiety have these feelings of being sent coded signals caused you?

Um... distress? I mean, I guess it's caused a little bit of anxiety, maybe? But really, it's not that bad. I don't want you to think I'm, like, falling apart over it or anything. 

It's more just... a distraction, I suppose? Like, I'll spend a little extra time rereading an email to see if I missed a hidden meaning, but then I just get back to work. I'm still getting all my assignments done and keeping up with my job, so it hasn't ruined my life or anything dramatic like that. 

I really try not to let it get to me too much. I mean, everyone gets a little stressed and overthinks things sometimes, right? I'm handling it okay, I think. Does it sound like I'm managing it alright to you? I really want to make sure I'm dealing with this the right way.
Have you changed your behavior in any way because of these perceived coded signals?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I haven't done anything drastic or anything like that. I'm definitely not, you know, confronting anyone or acting weird in class. 

I guess... well, maybe I'm just a little more careful about how I reply to emails? Like, I might take a few extra minutes to make sure my tone is perfectly professional, just in case they are testing me. But that's just being thorough, right? It's good to be professional in an MBA program anyway. 

I haven't stopped going to class or avoided anyone. I'm still participating and doing all the group work just like normal. I really don't want to make waves or seem difficult to work with. So, no, I haven't really changed my behavior in any big way. That's the right way to handle it, isn't it? Just keeping my head down and acting normal?
When you're completely alone and not trying to explain it to anyone, how convinced are you that the coded signals are real?

Um... well, if I'm being completely honest... when I'm totally alone, that's actually when it feels the most real. I mean, that's kind of why I came in to see you, even though I know it sounds really hard to explain. I just... I get completely convinced that my classmate and that startup advisor really are quietly coordinating opportunities for me. 

Like, I'll be sitting by myself reading over Slack messages or thinking about certain comments they made in class, and I just absolutely know they're coded signals about where my career is supposed to go. In those quiet moments, I don't doubt it at all. It just feels like a fact. 

But then I worry about how that sounds to you... I really don't want you to think I'm totally unreasonable or losing my grip. I'm just trying to answer you as honestly as I can. Is it okay that I get that convinced when I'm on my own? I really hope that doesn't make me sound too crazy... I'm doing the right thing by telling you this, right?
For how long have you felt completely convinced of the coded signals when you're alone?

Um... I'd say it's been about two months? Yeah, around two months. It started right around the time I began the part-time MBA prerequisite program. 

I've been trying to balance that with my regular operations manager job, so I've been pretty busy. I know sometimes when people get busy, their minds can kind of play tricks on them, so maybe it's just stress from trying to do both? I mean, it's totally normal to feel a little overwhelmed when you take on extra coursework, right? 

So, yeah, about two months of... well, of feeling this way when I'm by myself. But like I said, I'm still handling everything at work and school just fine. Two months isn't too long to be dealing with something like this, is it? I hope I didn't wait too long to talk to you about it.
Do you ever have moments when you're alone and you doubt that the coded signals are real?

Um... well... I guess if I'm really being honest, no. Not really. I mean, I try to tell myself I'm just overthinking it, because I know how it sounds. But when I'm just sitting there by myself, thinking about what they said in class or reading over those Slack messages... I don't really doubt it at all. 

I just... I get completely convinced that they really are quietly coordinating these opportunities for me. It just feels so clear that these are coded signals about where my career is supposed to go. 

I know that probably sounds... well, I know it sounds really hard to explain, and that's exactly why I came in. I just wanted to make sure I'm doing the right thing by talking to you about it. It's okay that I don't really doubt it when I'm alone, right? I'm just trying to be as honest as I can with you.
Have you had any other thoughts that you consider to be absolutely true, but that might seem unusual or hard to believe to others?

Um... no, actually. I mean, I've really tried to think about that, but... no, it's really just this one specific thing with the startup advisor and my classmate. 

Everything else in my life—like my job, my regular classes, my friends—my thoughts about all of that are completely normal. I'm definitely not, like, seeing signs everywhere or anything like that. It's really just this one isolated situation with my career opportunities. 

That's a good sign, right? Like, it means I'm mostly pretty grounded? I really hope it helps that it's just this one thing... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and being helpful.
Have you ever had any other thoughts that you were completely convinced were true, but might seem strange or unlikely to others?

Um... no, I really haven't. I know you just asked something kind of similar, and I... I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, but yeah, it's really just the one thing. 

I don't have any other strange thoughts or beliefs, I promise. Everything else is completely normal. I'm just a regular person trying to get through my MBA program and do a good job at work. I'm not, like, losing touch with reality in general or anything. 

I really try to keep a good head on my shoulders. It's just this one very specific situation that I'm completely convinced about. I hope that's okay? Like, I hope I'm answering your questions the right way. I really want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to figure this out.
Have you developed a comprehensive theory or explanation for why your classmate and the startup advisor are sending you coded signals?

Um... no, not really. I don't have, like, a big conspiracy board or anything like that. I really just figured they see my background in operations management and they're just quietly trying to guide me toward the right path? 

But I don't have a whole grand theory about the exact reasons why they're doing it this way. I just kind of trust that it's happening and take it day by day. 

I really hope that's okay to say... I just don't want you to think I'm sitting around making up wild stories in my head or obsessing over the details. I'm really just trying to follow the professional cues they're giving me. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it alright, I just want to make sure I'm not sounding, you know, completely unreasonable.
Are you having any difficulties in your relationships with friends, family, or colleagues because of your beliefs about the coded signals?

Um... well, maybe a little bit? I mean, I'm still showing up to everything, I promise. I haven't missed any days at work or skipped any classes or anything like that. I'm really trying my best to keep it all together.

But... I guess things have gotten a tiny bit tense lately. My manager at work, um, she started documenting some things... just some missed handoffs and what she called "unreliable follow-through." And then in my MBA program, my professor actually pulled me aside and questioned my judgment on a group assignment. 

I know that sounds bad, but it's not like I'm completely falling apart or anything! It's just... well, things were getting just strained enough with my work and school relationships that I thought, you know, maybe I should come talk to someone. Just to get a handle on it before it becomes a real problem. That was the right thing to do, right? Seeking help when things start to slip just a little? I really hope you don't think less of me for having a few hiccups at work... I'm usually a really good employee and student.
Have you started to avoid or limit interactions with your classmate or the startup advisor because of these perceived coded signals?

Um... no, not at all. I haven't been avoiding them. I mean, I actually try to make sure I'm around so I don't miss anything they might be trying to tell me. 

I'm still going to class, still going to the events where the advisor is... I really try to be professional about it. I don't want to come across as rude or, you know, unprofessional by avoiding people. I just kind of quietly pay attention when they're around. 

That's the right way to handle it, isn't it? Just keeping things normal and polite on the surface? I really try to make sure I'm acting appropriately in those settings. I definitely wouldn't just start hiding from them or anything like that.
Are you finding it harder to focus on your work or studies because of your thoughts about the coded signals?

Um... well, maybe just a tiny bit? But I'm really trying my hardest to stay on top of everything, I promise. 

I mean, sometimes when I'm trying to read a case study for class or, you know, finish up a report at work, my mind might wander just for a second... just thinking about what the signals might mean for my career path. But I always catch myself and get right back to work! I'm not, like, sitting at my desk staring at the wall for hours or anything like that. 

I really pride myself on being focused and getting my work done. It's just a little extra noise in the background sometimes, you know? But I'm managing it. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad manager or a bad student... it's normal to get a little distracted sometimes, right? As long as I'm still getting everything turned in?
Do you think there's any possibility that your classmate and the startup advisor are not actually sending you coded signals?

Um... well... I know it sounds really hard to explain, and maybe a little out there... but I've just been so completely convinced that they are. 

I mean, that's actually why I came in to talk to someone. Because part of me knows how it sounds to other people, but to me, it's just felt so real. Like, I really believed that my MBA classmate and that startup advisor were quietly coordinating opportunities for me. I'd see certain comments they'd make in class, or specific Slack messages, and I just... I felt certain they were coded signals about where my career is supposed to go. 

I know that probably sounds a little strange, right? But it's not like I'm crazy or anything... it's just that the connections felt so obvious to me at the time. I'm really trying to be open to the idea that maybe I misread things, though. That's what a reasonable person would do, isn't it? Question their own assumptions when things get a little strained? I really hope you don't think I'm completely losing touch with reality... I just got a little too caught up in trying to figure out my career path.
Have your beliefs about the coded signals changed at all since you first started noticing them two months ago?

Um... changed? Well, maybe a little? But honestly, they've mostly stayed the same since it all started. 

Like I mentioned before, I've just been so completely convinced that they're coordinating things for me. It's just... it's been this steady feeling that my classmate and the advisor are sending me these coded signals through their Slack messages or comments in class, pointing me toward the right career moves. 

I mean, I haven't really wavered from believing that's what's happening. It's just felt so consistent and real to me this whole time. But I am trying my best to keep an open mind now, like we talked about. I really want to be cooperative and figure this out. It's okay if it takes me a little time to adjust how I'm looking at things, right? I just want to make sure I'm approaching this the right way.
Do you think it's possible that you might be completely wrong about your classmate and the startup advisor sending you coded signals?

Um... gosh, well... I know I keep coming back to this, and I really don't want to sound stubborn. I want to be a good patient and just say yes, I'm completely wrong. I know that's probably what I'm supposed to say, right? 

But... like I was trying to explain earlier, that's exactly why I came in to see you in the first place. Because I've just been so, so completely convinced that they are quietly coordinating these opportunities for me. Even when I try to step back, when I think about those Slack messages or the specific things they say in class, my mind just immediately goes to how they have to be coded signals about where my career is supposed to go. 

I am really, really trying to see it from your perspective, I promise. It's just... it's a little scary to admit that something I believed so strongly might be entirely in my head. I hope you're not frustrated with me for struggling to just let it go completely... I'm doing my best to work with you on this, is that okay?
For how long have you been completely convinced that the coded signals are real when you're not trying to explain it to anyone?

Um... well, when I'm just by myself, not trying to explain it to anyone... I guess it's been about two months? 

That's when I started taking the prerequisite classes for the part-time MBA program, while still working my regular operations job. I was just really focused on trying to do well at both, you know? I wanted to make a good impression. And that's when it started feeling so real... like they were noticing my hard work and trying to guide me. 

Two months isn't that long in the grand scheme of things, right? I mean, it's just a short little phase while I was adjusting to a heavier workload. I'm sure lots of people get a little carried away when they're stressed and trying to succeed, don't they? I really hope that doesn't make me sound too unstable... I just wanted to do a good job.
Do you think the coded signals are part of a larger plan or scheme that you've figured out?

Um... a larger plan? Well... I guess that's sort of what I meant when I said they were coordinating opportunities for me. I wouldn't call it a... a scheme, though. That sounds so sinister, and I really don't think it's anything bad! 

It's just that I've been so sure that this classmate and the advisor are working together to guide me. Like, the specific comments they make in class, or the way they word things in Slack... I've just been so convinced that those are coded signals pointing me toward the right career moves. So, yes, I suppose I thought I had figured out their plan for my career. 

I know it probably sounds a bit silly when I say it out loud like that. I really don't want you to think I'm paranoid or anything like that. I just thought they were trying to be helpful and mentor me in their own unique way. That's a somewhat normal thing to misinterpret when you're really eager to advance in your career, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers...
